description: A "thinking" bar that announces its steps one by one and finally settles and calms down.
interactionNotes: The line reveals the steps one by one, with a soft shimmer sliding over the current text. When it finishes, a thin colored line advances, the text fades slightly, and it takes on the done color. If collapsing is enabled, a click collapses and expands it.

props.label: The text shown while it is working.
props.doneLabel: The text shown after it finishes; empty means the last step stays.
props.renderLabel: A full replacement for rendering the label.
props.glyph: The marker next to the text.
props.glyphColor: Color of the marker; empty means the same as the text color.
props.breathPeriod: Breathing period of the marker, in seconds.
props.shimmer: A sliding shimmer over the current text.
props.shimmerDuration: Duration of one shimmer cycle, in seconds.
props.settleDuration: Duration of the final settle, in milliseconds.
props.settleAfter: Finish by itself after how many seconds; zero means manual.
props.elapsed: Elapsed time; omit it to have it count on its own.
props.onSettle: When it settles, with the total duration.
props.className: Extra class on the component container.
props.style: Inline styles for the component container.

tips: Add steps to the list **one at a time**, not all at once. The component checks off each step except the last, so the "one-by-one checking" is only visible when the list also fills up one by one.
When the last step arrives, turn `working` off — that is the moment the last step gets its check, the header settles on "Thought for:", and (if `collapseOnSettle` is on) the list collapses.
Great for a chat assistant: fill the steps from real work so the user knows where they are.
If you give a timeout, it ends by itself after that — good for short, simulated tasks.
Turn the marker off if you already have a marker elsewhere and do not want two.
Do not take `breathDepth` above 0.6: the text's opacity goes from 1 to `1 - depth`, and above that the line effectively disappears.
If you build your own counter and rely on `tabular-nums`: it does not work on **Persian** digits. Peyda has matching glyphs for them. Put each digit in a fixed-width step.
